If your Apple CarPlay connection suddenly drops while you're driving, the problem may not lie with your iPhone, the cable, or the car itself.

Instead, it could be caused by radio interference.

A previous Axios report detailed a strange phenomenon in Boston, where drivers found their CarPlay or Android Auto connections interrupted when passing through specific locations. Similar 'signal dead zones' may exist in other cities, but no one has complained about them.

The CarPlay head unit cannot handle GPS navigation on its own; it maintains a direct connection with your iPhone via Bluetooth or Wi-Fi, then mirrors the display. Everything on the screen relies on your phone's internet connection and GPS satellite signals. When the wireless connection between the head unit and the phone is interfered with, navigation will fail and the connection may drop.

Mainframe's comment received the most likes

In Grapevine, Texas, I know of a specific stretch of road sandwiched between an oil depot and a nursing home where every wireless CarPlay system will crash when driving through. I've tried several vehicles, including ones with factory-installed wireless CarPlay, ones using wireless CarPlay adapters, and aftermarket audio systems—all of them get stuck on this stretch. Some systems recover after the interference passes, others don't. Even the latest Mercedes-Benz electric vehicles have this problem.

In the past ten years, I've only encountered this situation a few times.

Experts point out that nearby radio sources—especially signals in the 2.4GHz band—could be the source of the interference. In the case of Boston, the suspects may include point-to-point microwave links, broadcast antennas, or unlicensed transmitting devices.

The most important point is this: if you frequently lose your CarPlay connection at the same location, you may be driving through an invisible radio interference zone. This problem may not have a solution, but knowing the cause can save you a lot of time—no more endless searching for the reason, and no unnecessary repair appointments.
